predecessors.name: French First Republic
predecessors.text: the republic of the Convention, Belgium and the occupied left bank of the Rhine included

successors.name: French Consulate
successors.text: the whole republic after the coup of 18 Brumaire (9-10 November 1799)

ledger.x: 26 October 1795: the Directory takes over the Republic.
The Batavian Republic stays France's sister republic.
The left bank of the Rhine stays in French hands.
28 April 1796: Sardinia is knocked out of the war.
10 May 1796: Lombardy falls to Bonaparte.
October 1796: France retakes Corsica.
29 June 1797: Lombardy becomes the Cisalpine Republic.
29 June 1797: the Cisalpine Republic, a sister republic of France, is decreed at Milan.
14 June 1797: the Ligurian Republic is founded under French oversight.
17 October 1797: the Treaty of Campo Formio gives France the left bank of the Rhine.
17 October 1797: the left bank of the Rhine is annexed.
October 1797: the Ionian Islands pass from Venice to France.
1798: Mulhouse joins France.
1798: Malta is taken.
10 February 1798: the Roman Republic is proclaimed after Berthier occupies Rome.
12 April 1798: the Helvetic Republic is proclaimed.
2 July 1798: Bonaparte takes Alexandria and, with Egypt, the Nile valley.
26 August 1798: Geneva is made part of France.
December 1798: the armistice districts merge into the occupation of all Piedmont (bridging; the page gives no return of the 1796 districts).
6 December 1798: the French drive the king out of Piedmont.
1799: the French lose Piedmont.
26 January 1799: the Parthenopean Republic is proclaimed at Naples.
27 April 1799: the Austro-Russian army takes the Cisalpine Republic.
Summer 1799: the Roman Republic collapses.
Summer 1799: the Parthenopean Republic collapses with the other Italian sister republics after Novi (15 August 1799); the page gives no date for Naples.
9 November 1799: the coup of 18 Brumaire ends the Directory.

wars.name: War of the First Coalition (Directory years)
wars.outcome: Treaty of Basel with Prussia (5 April 1795) and Spain (22 July 1795); Bonaparte's Italian campaign, Cherasco (28 April 1796), Lodi (10 May 1796), Campo Formio (17 October 1797), which gave France the left bank of the Rhine, Belgium and the Ionian Islands.

wars.name: Anglo-Corsican Kingdom and the recovery of Corsica
wars.outcome: British evacuation on 11 October 1796; the French reconquered Bastia on 19 October 1796.

wars.name: French invasion of Egypt
wars.outcome: The fleet sailed on 19 May 1798, took Malta and captured Alexandria on 2 July 1798; the expedition stays in Egypt after the Directory (to 1801).

wars.name: War of the Second Coalition
wars.outcome: 'The war began on 29 November 1798' (the page's wording); Jourdan defeated at Ostrach and Stockach (25 March 1799), Moreau at Cassano (27 April 1799), Joubert at Novi (15 August 1799), after which the Italian sister republics collapsed; Italian campaigns…

certainty.note: Metropolitan France and the annexed Belgium are administrative lines; the Rhineland (sharp only from Campo Formio, 17 October 1797), the Italian occupations, the Armistice of Cherasco districts and Egypt are fronts or garrisons and soft.

sources.title: Italian campaigns of the French Revolutionary Wars
